label: paragraph_title
text: MACAO'S TYPHOON.

label: paragraph_title
text: 2,000 LIVES LOST YESTERDAY?

label: text
text: Fishing Fleet Missing at Sea..

label: text
text: GUNBOAT DAMAGED: BUSINESS STOPPED THE WHOLE DAY.

label: text
text: Considerable damage to buildings and shipping and loss of life is feared to have occurred at Macao where the typhoon struck with severe force yesterday after blowing practically the whole day.

label: text
text: The entire fishing fleet, numbering some 700 junks, is reported to have been out at the time and in the absence of news up to a late hour yesterday evening it is believed that these have all been lost with the occupants on board.

label: text
text: PRICE, $3.00 Per Month.

label: text
text: "The s.s. 'Kinshan' and 'Tung' On" which arrived in Hong Kong this forenoon, were at Macao the whole of yesterday, but beyond experiencing a stiff blow those aboard knew very little of what took place on land and sea.

label: paragraph_title
text: Flying Debris.

label: text
text: When the wind increased in force the boats were ordered to draw away from the wharf, and from their position they were able to see only a few junks ashere near the Praya and the usual debris flying from the tops of buildings.

label: text
text: During the voyage this morning one of the vessels observed a number of junk without masts, drifting in the distance.

label: text
text: A report by the Customs at Macao this morning was to other effect that a passenger junk was on the rocks outside Macao. All aboard, numbering 68, have been drowned.

label: paragraph_title
text: Gunboat in Distress.

label: text
text: According to what ship's officers heard this morning after their arrival in Hong Kong, a rumour was current here that 2,000 lives had been lost in the typhoon.

label: text
text: The Portuguese gunboat "Macao" had a distressing time in the typhoon. When seem after the typhoon her foremost was missing, having been blown away. It is believed that damage was also done to other parts of the vessel.

label: text
text: [Note: Each junk in the important industry of fishing at Macao employs an average of 15 persons, mostly men. These boats sometimes venture out, often at night, to 30 to 4 miles from shore.]

label: text
text: Until accurate information is received from Macao, it is difficult to estimate the death roll and the damage done to shipping and buildings.

label: text
text: Hong Kong's Sympathy.

label: text
text: Other typhoon reports, together with later local developments, will be found elsewhere in this issue, and in the shipping section (pages 4 and 5).

label: text
text: It is understood that the Hong Kong Government will send a message of condolence to H.E. the Governor of Macao on the loss of life sustained.

label: paragraph_title
text: Prediction Borne Out..

label: text
text: The Observatory report on the typhoon, issued yesterday, predicted that if the typhoon maintained its course, it would strike the coast near Macao.

label: text
text: This appears to have been borne out.

label: text
text: Very high wind velocity was recorded and the "glass" was very low.

label: paragraph_title
text: BAG SNATCHERS.

label: paragraph_title
text: ATTEMPT AT GARDEN ROAD.

label: text
text: THIEF CAUGHT.

label: text
text: While Mrs. Hickey was returning from the Cathedral along Garden Road on Saturday, a Chinese youth tugged at her handbag, but failed to get it. Mrs. Parsons and Mrs. Hall were also with her at the time.

label: text
text: Sergeant Hopkins had his attention drawn to the runaway and chased him on his motor cycle. The youth attempted to get away by running across the parade ground, but the Sergeant ran on foot and caught him as he was getting through a hole in the railing near the matshed.

label: text
text: Defendant, who had two previous convictions, was sentenced to eight months' hard labour and to receive 15 strokes.

label: text
text: A small-boy who was pointed out by the defendant as a member of the same gang was ordered 12 strokes by the Magistrate.

label: text
text: In the inner harbour (sheltered) the effect was not badly felt but side it was rough even at sunset.

label: text
text: The wide radius of the typhoon may also have had an adverse effect on the fishing fleet.

label: text
text: Hiding All Day.

label: text
text: (From An Occasion Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Waves even on the inner harbour were dashed so high that some of the shops near the river front were inundated.

label: text
text: Early in the morning, the blow was felt and the storm had not subsided till nearly 7 pm.

label: text
text: Communications were almost entirely interrupted.

label: text
text: The supply of electricity seems to have been affected as even lights in several places were not in operation last night.

label: text
text: People hid indoors most of the day, having laid in supplies at sunrise.

label: text
text: Business establishments were closed throughout the day.

label: text
text: There may have been isolated cases of collapse of old buildings brought about by the storm.

label: text
text: Severe Wind Force.

label: text
text:
No fresh stocks of provisions
rived yesterday and prices, were
high this morning.

label: text
text:
Even in some of the narrowest streets the wind howled all day.
On the Praia Grande, the wind force must have been well over 100 miles an hour during the height of the typhoon about 8.30 a.m.

label: text
text: The centre of the cyclone passed very close.

label: text
text: In extent of lives lost, yesterday's typhoon is probably worse than that of 1923—when there was ample warning—but few, if any, perished ashore.

label: paragraph_title
text: FIERCE STRUGGLE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
ALLEGED ASSAULT ON
CONSTABLE.

label: text
text: SESSIONS SEQUEL.

label: text
text: An assault on an Indian constable and the taking of his revolver by two men who accosted him at Yaumati early in the morning on August 10 was considered at the Sessions this morning before Mr. Justice Wood.

label: text
text: Mr. A. Dyer Ball stated that the men had engaged the constable in conversation and then seized him from the front and also from behind. A violent struggle ensued in the course of which the constable sustained injuries to his head and arms and had a tooth broken. One of his two assailants got away with the revolver and holster but the constable held on to the other and when assistance came from a water police cox-swain he was able to overpower

label: text
text: The second prisoner was arrested eleven days later as he was about to leave for Macao. The revolver was found shortly after the struggle on a heap of iron nearby.

label: text
text: In statements made after arrest the two prisoners admitted being on the scene. The first prisoner indicated the second as the man who had made the assault. The second prisoner admitted taking the revolver and assaulting the policeman.

label: text
text: At the court proceedings, however, both prisoners had amended their version of affairs, it was pointed out.

label: text
text: This two men pleaded not guilty this morning.

label: text
text: The whole of the morning was occupied with hearing evidence. This afternoon, His Honour (Mr. Justice Wood) will sum up for the benefit of the jury.

label: text
text: Mr. W. Goldsmidt, who for the last twenty years has been connected with Messrs. Ullmann and Co., was entertained to a farewell dinner by a few friends at the Cafe Restaurant. Parlien on Monday evening prior to his departure from Hong Kong on a well-earned retirement.

label: paragraph_title
text: BOYCOTT END.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Canton's Reasons For
Settlement.

label: text
text: INTERVIEW WITH OFFICIAL

label: text
text: Scheme to Demobilise Strike

label: paragraph_title
text: Picket5

label: text
text: In the interval between the initial announcement and the actual termination of the boy-cott, rumourists are still busy as to the outcome.

label: text
text: Advice from Canton is that the native merchants are practically unanimous that "communications will be restored by October 1, or a few days afterwards. More than that, cannot be definitely stated.

label: text
text: In Hong Kong, on the other hand, a degree of pessimism prevails. The belief is that while normal conditions will be brought in, on appearances, there will remain.

label: text
text: main a boycott of Hong Kong and British ships and cargo. Those who adhere to this opinion main-

label: text
text: tain that Canton will not voluntarily call off the "strike" without obtaining concessions or terms and until such are settled, trade will still be restricted. That, however, remains to be seen.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” commends to its“readers the article (reproduced on Saturday) from the “Canton Gazette.” Against this it should be borne in mind that

label: text
text: Mr. Eugene Chen has made no further pronouncement about the projected new taxes on luxuries, imports and exports.

label: paragraph_title
text: Sense of Uneasiness.

label: text
text: "A sense of uneasiness is felt at the absence of a further statement (firstly) as to whether the termination will depend on the institution of the level and (secondly) as to whether there will only be resumption of communications without the former trade."

label: text
text: According to a vernacular paper, this official is quoted as having denied rumours that the settlement was contingent on an understanding having been arrived at with Britain in regard to (a) a loan on the railway scheme as detailed at the peace conference (b) the allocation of the Customs Surplus of the south of China to Canton and (c) that the new taxes be collected through the Maritime Customs.

label: text
text: The reply of the official, as given, is that the Nationalist Government has now extended its scope to such an extent that a boycott is undesirable in general interests and that the presence of abnormal conditions in the "home area" is undesirable.

label: paragraph_title
text: Prosperity and Peace.

label: text
text: As to the luxury and other luxes, the official is said to have maintained that their collection was outside of the scope of the Customs and that the co-operation was merely desired to ensure smooth and rapid working.

label: text
text: An unofficial view expressed is that the Canton Government has decided to end the boycott as it is now felt that former trade connections must be resumed to bring about prosperity and peace in Kwangtung.

label: text
text: Semi-official schemes have been advanced, and in some cases approved, for demobillsing the strikers, and pickets. Such comprise (a) each man to be given a Government bounty of $50 to seek employment (b) those unable to find work to be assisted (or recommended) to Kwangsi, Hunan and Hupeh, or to be attached to factories, public offices, etc. (c) pickets to be drafted into military service corps.

label: text
text: Conflicting reports continue to come in about picket activities in various parts of the province.

label: text
text: Attractive Pay.

label: text
text: In Canton there has been a considerable decrease in the numbers on duty, but batches have still made surprise appearances here and there.

label: text
text: General Ho Ying-yum of Swatow is stated to have naked the leading unions to supply him with 200 pickets, for transport service on the Fukden front at attractive rates of pay. Pickets there have not been disbanded yet but are in communication with Canton headquarters. Continued at foot of next column.

label: paragraph_title
text: OWNERS BLAMED.

label: paragraph_title
text: Government and the Coal Crisis.

label: text
text: WHERE MINERS ERRED..

label: text
text: Mr. Cook Now Preaches “Organised Retreat.”

label: paragraph_title
text: London. Sept. 27.

label: text
text: Both Houses of “Parliament meet this afternoon to authorise for the sixth time the Emergency Powers Act”

label: text
text: An interesting and important debate in the House of Commons is expected.

label: text
text: Mr. Cook predicted over the week-end that the twenty-second week of the stoppage would be the most critical in the history of the Miners' Federation.

label: text
text:
The miners' proposals, just rejected, were a distinct concession, but the Miners' Executive realise that they must go farther.
Mr. Cook has been telling the Somerset miners that, he believed in "Organised Retreat." "We have got to compromise. I wish we had not to compromise, but it must be forced." He added that whatever the Miners' conference on Wednesday decided, he would carry out or he would "clear out."—Reuter.

label: text
text: (Continued on Page 7.)

label: text
text: At Samchun station (just over the New Territory border), fewer pickets are on duty but "passes" and baggage are still being examined.

label: text
text: There is 'no news from Chin-shup' (on the Macao frontier). These at Lappa (facing Macao harbour) were still on duty during the week-end.

label: text
text: Whampoa Dispersal Camp.

label: text
text: Ndr is there any change in the attitude of the pickets at Kongmoon.

label: text
text: The same report says that all outport pickets will be, asked to return to Canton for final demobilisation.

label: text
text:
Those who leave voluntarily or join the service corps will be sent away. The remainder may be removed to Whampoa, as the dormitories and eating rooms in Canton city are being discontinued as from October 1, Should it be necessary, accommodation may be provided at Whampoa in the nature of a dispersal camp.
Interviewed by the “China Mail,” a Chinese owner of important river shipping interests said that he preferred to wait till all was clear. He did not doubt the official communique sent out by Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: Waiting for a Lead.

label: text
text:
His boats had remained idle for a good many months, manned by skeleton crews on reduced pay. To obtain full complements was easy. It was, however, necessary to send ships into dock for overhaul before taking up the run again. If there was no prospect of continued business, the outlay would not be worth while.
Owners of “outside” river steamers, the speaker remarked, were waiting for a lead from the Steamboat Co. It would be unprofitable for the smaller boats to go up and anchor in the stream on the offchance of picking up passengers and freight. They had to work on a regular schedule and go alongside a wharf. Until the

label: text
text: go alongside a whari. Until the Steamboat Co.'s ships used their wharves again, he did not think that the other boats would rush in.

label: paragraph_title
text: Funds for Strikers

label: text
text: [From Our Own Correspondent.]

label: text
text: Pakkai, Kongmoon, Sept. 24. A mass meeting and parade has

label: text
text: been held at Kongmoon city to raise funds for Strike Headquarters in Canton.

label: text
text: All labour organisations and public offices observed the day as a holiday.

label: text
text: This was prior to the arrival of news of the “official settlement” announced by the Canton Government.

label: paragraph_title
text: COUNTER-OFFENSIVE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Sun Chuan-fang Claims Victory.

label: text
text: SOUTHERN ARMY REPULSED.

label: text
text: Decisive Battle May be Fought This Week.

label: text
text: Further victories for Marshal Sun Chuan-fang are claimed in the latest despatches from the "war zone" in Kiangsi.

label: text
text: Although the reports are deemed reliable, it should be borne in mind that the majority emanate from Shanghai, which is in the hands of the allies.

label: text
text: At two points, the Nationalists are reported to have been repulsed. The number of rifles captured (several thousand) may be exaggerated:

label: text
text: Another point of note is that the southern troops now fighting 'n Kiangsi are comparatively "fresh," not having been engaged in the Hunan and Hupeh operations.

label: text
text: They are the 2nd. 3rd and 6th Armies, comprising mostly Hunane and Yunnanese men, formerly mercenaries who migrated to Kwangtung when the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen was fighting Chan Kwingming.

label: text
text:
Did Dictator Have Doubts?
Could General Chang Kai-shek have doubted their "ability, as armies, when he left them in the rear, while he pushed on to Hankow in an earlier stage of the war?

label: text
text:
These three armies were stationed between Kwangtung's northern boundary and Yochow.
Latterly they marched eastwards into Kiangsi, meeting little resistance until Nanchang was taken.

label: text
text:
Then Sun Chuan-fang seems to have decided to fight in earnest.
The divisions which re-took Nanchang (capital of Kiangsi) claim to have driven off the ex-mercenaries to some distance west and south of Nanchang. They also maintain that they are maintaining their counter-offensive and that the Nationalists are falling back on the Kiangsi-Hunan border.

label: text
text: In the north of Kiangsi, two of Sun Chuan-fang's expeditions moved up the Yangtse River, and landed at different places. They immediately went into action against the Cadets (Ist Nationalist Army, one division) and other troops from the 7th and 8th armies which had been deflected from the Wu-Han sector.

label: text
text:
Both expeditions are reported to have pushed back the southerners. It is even boasted that the allies will be marching on Hupeh province (and Hankow), very shortly.
However, the southerners are moving more troops eastwards to meet Sun Chuan-fang. Their objective is the port of Klukiang, further down the Yangtse.

label: text
text:
In view of the foregoing, a decisive battle is due this week.
To the North of Hankow, the position is still obscure.

label: text
text: Hampered by raids by General Fan Chung-iao's White Wolf Cubs (Red Spears), Wu Pei-fu's main strength was retreating northwards away from the Yangtze. But one detachment has broken through, southwards, on a flank, and is believed to have reached a point on the Yangtze considerably above Hankow.

label: text
text: Southerners are still moving up the Hankow-Peking Railway to take up new territory adjoining Honan province.

label: text
text:
There has been nothing to report on the Kwantung-Fuklen front.
Chang Tso-lin (Fengtien party) is still promising Wu Pei-fu and Sun Chuan-fang help but he seems to be consolidating his hold on Peking and getting his nominee to become Premier (or even the new President) in place of Wu Pei-fu's men.

label: text
text:
Shanghai Sept. 27.
Fengtien authorities took over the Peking garrison this morning and assumed direct responsibility for the maintenance of order in the capital.—Reuter.

label: text
text: One Chinese case of "enteric" over (typhoid) in the city was reported to the Medical Officer of Health on Sunday.
